near_miss.lead: great cares keep a hero from sleep: ON storar ahygior ... andvǫcor miclar ~ OIr imṡníma móra ... coná reilcset cotlud dó (Fer Diad)
near_miss.why_not: Congruent motif (anxiety the night/winter before a fateful act prevents sleep) but no cognate material: mór/stórr, imṡním/áhyggja, cotlud/andvaka are unrelated; universal narrative motif.

near_miss.lead: night + sleep: ON sváfo um nóttina / ganga at sofa ~ Gk ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον ~ Lat nocte in somnis
near_miss.why_not: Only *nokʷt- and *swep- co-occurring in narrative of going to bed; ON prose phrasing is plain saga style, Greek is 'sleepless nights' (opposite sense), Latin is a dream formula. Generic.

anchors: xcl:MH_1_1_06_Yeghishe ed. page 579 - PDF page 59 (word id 9376)
near_miss.lead: kinship enumeration father/mother/brother(/daughter): ORu брат брату ... отьць сынови ... мати дъчери (kin do not pity kin in famine) ~ RV pitā́ mātā́ bhrā́taraḥ (kin disown the gambler)
near_miss.why_not: Cognate kin terms in a list are expected anywhere; the ORu polyptoton (brother to brother, neighbour to neighbour) is a biblical/apocalyptic topos (Mic 7:6, Mt 10:21) in a Christian chronicle; RV lacks the polyptoton. ON pivots are plain genealogy.

near_miss.lead: copula + daughter + sister self-identification: ON ec em konongs dóttir oc konongs systir ~ AV asurāṇāṃ duhitā asi sā devānām asi svasā / śraddhāyā duhitā ... svasa ṛṣīṇāṃ
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate triple (*h1es-, *dhugh2ter-, *swesor-) in same frame, but a woman's natal status is naturally stated by father and brother; contexts differ (princess protesting a low marriage vs. a deified plant's divine kinship in a charm); also byliny сестра родная, дочи царская by search. Too generic to defend.

near_miss.lead: *h2ews- + *wodr: ON ausa vatni (pagan name-giving sprinkling) ~ Gk ἀφύσσασθαι ὕδωρ
near_miss.why_not: Different syntax (ON instrumental 'sprinkle with water' vs. Gk accusative 'draw water') and context (ritual naming vs. watering at a ship); 'scoop water' is the verb's natural object; ἀφύσσω's link to *h2ews- is itself uncertain. Search: ON 'vatni ausinn' is frequent (Egils s., Laxdæla, Rígsþula jósu vatni) but has no matching collocation elsewhere.

near_miss.lead: beasts of battle: skaldic let hraufnom holld flæmingia golldit, gaf ... at drecka bloð
near_miss.why_not: Known feeding-the-carrion-beasts motif (recalled), but the Irish partner is about cairns/pillar stones after battle, no congruent wording and no cognates.

near_miss.lead: asking a stranger his name and lineage: ON spurði hvert nafn ... var, ætt eða óðli / spyrr hann at nafni oc ætt
near_miss.why_not: Only *h1nomn- shared; Herodotus/RV partners are 'whose name was', not a question; the name-and-kin inquiry is universal.

near_miss.lead: no lead (oath-binding, conversion offer, marriage treaty)
near_miss.why_not: Shared roots only (bróðir/брат, konungr, dóttir/duhitā); no collocation.
